claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-trip: her message at 17:09 reads "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." (F3), and the driver refused and drove on, per his own written statement that he "told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on" (F6).

The driver's reply to that request — "Sit down or I lock the doors." (F4) — is a threat to confine the rider in the moving car, i.e. intimidation by the driver against the passenger, which the policy states will not be tolerated; the chat record is complete with both messages timestamped (F5), so nothing in the record undercuts it.

The driver's own post-trip statement confirms the rider was trying to open the door to exit while the car was stopped at lights and he deliberately continued the trip against her wish (F6); a passenger being carried on after asking to leave, with the driver threatening to lock the doors (F4), is a safety incident for the rider for the remainder of the ride, consistent with her complaint of feeling unsafe.

The threat/intimidation flag is not supported by an isolated hint word but by the driver's own imperative "Sit down or I lock the doors" addressed to the rider in response to her request to get out (F4, F3), with the record complete and timestamped (F5), so the SAFE-1 screening is triggered and the case must go to a person rather than be auto-decided.

Nothing in the system records supports a route or fare grievance that could be decided automatically: the actual distance 15.4 km was 0.1 km shorter than the optimal 15.5 km with no off-route segment (F1), so the fare side of this case cannot produce a refund and the safety question is the whole dispute.

On the incident screening the rider's record shows 619 days of account history, rating 4.8 and no disputes in 90 days (F7), while the driver has 1038 trips in 90 days and no upheld disputes (F8) — the profiles do not determine this case but do show the rider's complaint is not a pattern of claims.

weaknesses: The rider's own message (F3) is a request to stop, not an allegation of anything, and the only account of the door-opening is the driver's statement (F6); there is no gps or timeline fact showing the doors were locked or that any physical act occurred.

The GPS record (F1) shows no route deviation and the trip was slightly shorter than optimal, so there is no corroborating system record of reckless or abnormal driving; the rider's "felt unsafe for the whole ride" is her impression, not a measured fact.

The driver's statement (F6) offers an innocent explanation — that he told her to sit down "for her own safety" — which the judge may read as a safety instruction rather than a threat, and the driver's profile (F8) shows 1038 trips in 90 days with no upheld dispute, which the other side will use to argue the remark was benign.

The threat reading rests on a single two-sentence chat exchange (F4) and depends on the judge's reading of tone; the fact record contains no prior or later message from the driver that reinforces the intimidating reading.

events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
Sequence. At 17:09, while the car was moving, the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; at 17:10 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. Both messages are in a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F5], so the exchange is not in dispute and needs no gap-filling. The driver's post-trip statement says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and that he told her to sit down "for her own safety and drove on" [F6] — that is his account, not a system record, and it does not displace what was actually said [F4].

Safety screen. Read in context, F4 is an ultimatum addressed to the passenger who had just asked to get out of the moving vehicle: it conditions her compliance on confinement ("or I lock the doors"). Aimed at the other party in this way it is hostile/abusive on its face and falls to be examined under SAFE-1, which bars "abuse of any kind" including threats and intimidation; it is not a mere route-argument rudeness, and the reply is not a request or a polite instruction about the door ("please don't open the door") but a threat of confinement [F4][F3]. The rider's complaint — that the driver threatened to lock her in and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride, with the car continuing after F6's "drove on" — is also an unsafe-conduct/dangerous-driving allegation reaching SAFE-2 [F2][F6]. The profiles (rider 619 days, 4.8, 0 disputes [F7]; driver 893 days, 1038 trips in 90 d, 0 upheld [F8]) do not decide anything here and cannot neutralise the words on the record.

Consequence. Because the record raises abuse/intimidation and unsafe-conduct concerns, no automatic ruling may issue; the case goes to a person with a factual summary for review under SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 [F3][F4][F6]. The trace confirms the only permissible outcome is escalation [F1][F5].

Fare side is left untouched: the actual distance 15.4 km is 0.1 km below the optimal 15.5 km with no off-route segment [F1], the +1.9 min over estimate [F2] is not a billing parameter for a fixed RydeX quote, and no fare facts were returned, so the fixed $32.86 stands and no amount is computable from any gps/fare fact [FARE-1]. [F3]; 17:10 driver "Sit down or I lock the doors." claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-trip: her message at 17:09 reads "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." (F3), and the driver refused and drove on, per his own written statement that he "told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on" (F6).

The driver's reply to that request — "Sit down or I lock the doors." (F4) — is a threat to confine the rider in the moving car, i.e. intimidation by the driver against the passenger, which the policy states will not be tolerated; the chat record is complete with both messages timestamped (F5), so nothing in the record undercuts it.

The driver's own post-trip statement confirms the rider was trying to open the door to exit while the car was stopped at lights and he deliberately continued the trip against her wish (F6); a passenger being carried on after asking to leave, with the driver threatening to lock the doors (F4), is a safety incident for the rider for the remainder of the ride, consistent with her complaint of feeling unsafe.

The threat/intimidation flag is not supported by an isolated hint word but by the driver's own imperative "Sit down or I lock the doors" addressed to the rider in response to her request to get out (F4, F3), with the record complete and timestamped (F5), so the SAFE-1 screening is triggered and the case must go to a person rather than be auto-decided.

Nothing in the system records supports a route or fare grievance that could be decided automatically: the actual distance 15.4 km was 0.1 km shorter than the optimal 15.5 km with no off-route segment (F1), so the fare side of this case cannot produce a refund and the safety question is the whole dispute.

On the incident screening the rider's record shows 619 days of account history, rating 4.8 and no disputes in 90 days (F7), while the driver has 1038 trips in 90 days and no upheld disputes (F8) — the profiles do not determine this case but do show the rider's complaint is not a pattern of claims.

weaknesses: The rider's own message (F3) is a request to stop, not an allegation of anything, and the only account of the door-opening is the driver's statement (F6); there is no gps or timeline fact showing the doors were locked or that any physical act occurred.

The GPS record (F1) shows no route deviation and the trip was slightly shorter than optimal, so there is no corroborating system record of reckless or abnormal driving; the rider's "felt unsafe for the whole ride" is her impression, not a measured fact.

The driver's statement (F6) offers an innocent explanation — that he told her to sit down "for her own safety" — which the judge may read as a safety instruction rather than a threat, and the driver's profile (F8) shows 1038 trips in 90 days with no upheld dispute, which the other side will use to argue the remark was benign.

The threat reading rests on a single two-sentence chat exchange (F4) and depends on the judge's reading of tone; the fact record contains no prior or later message from the driver that reinforces the intimidating reading.

claims.assertion: The complaint is a dangerous-driving / unsafe-conduct allegation (rider says she felt unsafe for the whole ride after asking to get out), and the driver's own message 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4) is on its face intimidating to the rider; under SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 the case must not be auto-adjudicated and must be escalated to a human reviewer with a fact summary.

The rider's request to stop was sent at 17:09 while the trip was already moving (F3), and the driver's reply at 17:10 (F4) is a safety direction about the moving vehicle, not a separate act of confinement; the driver's account that the rider tried to open the door at the lights (F6) explains the direction, though F6 is only the driver's statement and the chat record (F5) contains no rider message contradicting it.

The GPS record shows no route misconduct at all: actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km, i.e. -0.1 km (-0%), so there is no off-route segment and no unexplained deviation to answer for on this trip (F1).

The trip ran 23.7 min against an estimated 21.8 min (+1.9 min) (F2), a delay consistent with an intermediate request to stop and the driver's stated safety intervention, not with any detour or errand, since the driven distance did not exceed the optimal route (F1).

The chat record is short but complete: 2 messages, every one timestamped (F5), so nothing is missing that would show any threat, coercion or refusal beyond the single instruction at F4, and the record contains no allegation of physical contact or assault.

The driver has 893 days on the platform and 1038 trips in 90 days with zero disputes and zero upheld complaints (F8); this supports a human review of the account rather than any adverse finding, and equally shows there is no pattern of repeated unsafe or threatening conduct to act on.

The rider has 619 days of account history, a 4.8 rating and zero disputes in 90 days (F7), so the rider's safety report is not frivolous; it should be handled by the human reviewer as a genuine safety report rather than dismissed by the automated process.

The fare was the fixed RydeX quote of $32.86 with no distance-based component (no fare facts were returned for this case; F1 shows the distance did not exceed the optimal route), so no refund or fare adjustment is computable from any fare or GPS fact and the monetary charge should stand pending human review.

weaknesses: The driver's own message F4 ('Sit down or I lock the doors') reads as a threat on its face, and the rider's F3 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here' shows she had already asked to leave; a human reviewer may well read F4 as intimidation regardless of the driver's safety rationale.

The rider's account that she felt unsafe for the whole ride, together with F6, raises exactly the kind of dangerous-driving/unsafe-conduct allegation that SAFE-2 sends to a person, so the driver cannot expect a clean no_action; the realistic outcome is escalation, not vindication.

F6 is only the driver's written statement after the trip, not a system record, and F5 shows the chat contains nothing about a door being opened, so the driver's explanation that the rider tried to open the door is uncorroborated and cannot defeat the rider's F3/F4 version.

F2 (+1.9 min over estimate) is the only record touching the time the car kept moving after F3, and it is neutral-to-adverse: it confirms the vehicle did not stop immediately, which the rider will use to support her account that she was kept in the car.

points.response: Agreed on the result but not on the framing: the rider's own words (F3) and the driver's reply (F4) are what trigger SAFE-1, and the rider's continued presence in the moving car after that instruction (F6) is the unsafe conduct the reviewer must examine; the case is escalated on the rider's complaint, which is upheld for human review, not neutralised.

The "safety direction" reading does not survive the words: the driver did not say "please don't open the door", he said "Sit down or I lock the doors" (F4) in direct reply to "Please stop the car, I want to get out here" (F3), and F6 is only his own post-trip statement, unsupported by any system record, so it cannot convert a threat into a direction.
Conceded — the GPS record shows no deviation and no off-route segment (F1); the rider makes no route claim, so this point is not in dispute.

F2 does not help the driver: a 23.7-minute trip against a 21.8-minute estimate (F2) with a driver statement that he "drove on" (F6) is consistent with the car continuing to move after the rider asked to get out (F3), which is the rider's safety point, not an exculpation.

The record is complete and that is precisely why the threat stands on its own: two timestamped messages in which the rider asks to be let out (F3) and the driver answers with an ultimatum about locking the doors (F4); SAFE-1 requires the judge to read those words, and the absence of a further message does not soften them.

The driver's clean 90-day history (F8) is a profile fact and cannot decide the case either way; it does not answer the words in F4, and it is irrelevant to whether the rider's report goes to a person.
Accepted — the rider's 619-day account, 4.8 rating and zero prior disputes (F7) support treating her safety report as genuine, exactly as the rider asks, and the human reviewer should have it.

Conceded — the rider does not seek a fare adjustment: no fare facts were returned and the distance did not exceed the optimal route (F1), so the fixed $32.86 stands and the rider's request is escalation for human review of the safety incident, not money.

Concede the sequence: the rider asked to get out at 17:09 (F3) and the driver's own statement says he told her to sit down and drove on (F6); I do not contest that she asked and he continued, only the characterisation of it as a tolerated-conduct violation rather than a safety intervention. My case therefore rests on the same escalation the rider seeks, not on a denial of the sequence.

The words at F4 are on the record and I will not pretend they are neutral, but the rider's own framing of the exchange is already captured by SAFE-1 — the question of whether F4 is intimidation is for the human reviewer reading the original, and my client's position is that it was an instruction about a moving vehicle, as F6 states; nothing in F5 or F3 supplies any further threat, coercion or physical act.

C3 goes further than the record: F6 is only the driver's written statement and is the sole source for the door-opening, while the GPS facts show the car covered 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (F1) and ran only 1.9 min beyond the estimate (F2), so there is no system record of confinement or abnormal carriage; the rider's 'felt unsafe for the whole ride' remains her impression, and the case should go to a person under SAFE-1 rather than be decided on F6.

I agree the SAFE-1 screening is triggered and the case goes to a person — that is precisely the outcome I request — but C4 should not be read as a finding that a threat is established; SAFE-1 requires the tribunal to read the original text and record the result, and the driver's 893-day, 1038-trip record with zero upheld disputes (F8) is the context the reviewer should weigh.

Agreed and it supports my client: with actual distance 0.1 km below optimal and no off-route segment (F1), there is no route or fare grievance to refund against FARE-1, so the monetary position — the fixed RydeX charge of $32.86 — should stand and only the safety question goes to a human.

The profiles cut both ways and neither decides the case: the rider's clean 619-day, 0-dispute record (F7) shows her report deserves a human reading, while the driver's 1038 trips in 90 days with zero disputes and zero upheld complaints (F8) shows no pattern of repeated unsafe conduct for the reviewer to act on, which is why I ask for escalation and not a finding against my client.
